A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same semantic structure-aware generative attack. All pages, including Appendices A-C, are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original cross-model, cross-domain and cross-task attack experiments, component and block ablations, purification evaluations and three random-seed trials in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds GPT zero-shot classification and LLaVA image-captioning results in Tables S9-S10.

M1.justification: The EMA teacher, early-block hinge-based feature distillation, adversarial objective and teacher-based inference remain unchanged. The U-Net bottleneck adaptation was already documented in v1 Appendix A; the new evaluations do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: V4 expands evaluation beyond the retained classification, segmentation and detection settings to GPT zero-shot classification on ImageNet-R and ImageNet-1K, and MSCOCO image captioning with LLaVA. ImageNet-R adds represented data, while caption generation introduces substantially different task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding existing comparisons retain CDA, LTP, BIA, GAMA, FACL and PDCL. The new GPT and LLaVA evaluations compare BIA with BIA plus the proposed components; they introduce new targets, not new attack comparators or changes to existing comparator membership.

E3.justification: The new evaluations introduce zero-shot GPT testing with 400 random images and prompted captioning with LLaVA 1.5-7B/13B, scored using BLEU-4, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr and SPICE. Existing training and benchmark protocols remain unchanged. Figure S10 additionally specifies a 0.2 visualization threshold, although the retained appendix formula still uses zero, leaving that setting internally inconsistent.

E4.justification: Table 7 revises the cross-domain block-distillation ablation, including the relative ordering of mid- and late-block distillation. Figure S10 replaces examples and feature-difference maps in the existing analysis of where perturbations emerge. The component, surrogate-layer and hyperparameter ablation designs are retained.

E5.justification: The same three seed trials and aggregate uncertainty values appear in v1 Table S9 and v4 Table S11. V4 newly identifies these summaries explicitly as mean plus or minus standard deviation. This clarifies uncertainty reporting without establishing additional runs or new statistical tests.

E6.justification: New Table S9 reports GPT attack results, including BIA versus BIA-plus-ours accuracy of 5.00% versus 1.25% on GPT-4o-mini/ImageNet-1K. New Table S10 reports lower caption scores with ours for LLaVA-7B, but equal or higher scores for 13B. Table 7 also changes cross-domain early/mid/all accuracies from 45.86/48.07/49.44 to 47.10/50.95/51.13; early remains best. The purification and seed-trial values are retained.

T1.justification: The objectives, EMA formulation, evaluation-set definitions, ACR definition and appendix pooling/difference-map equations remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems or proofs appear. The changed Figure S10 threshold concerns empirical visualization rather than a revised theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: analysis of early generator semantics, the Mean Teacher and feature-distillation framework, and complementary evaluation using ACR. The added experiments extend supporting evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations of purification results, training stability and zero-shot attack failures, including conjectured interference with already effective generators and a possible capacity ceiling. The original limitations paragraph is merely moved. The new CLIP discussion lacks its referenced table, and the purification discussion misstates several trends in retained Table S8.

D1.justification: V4 supplies the captioning prompt, 'Provide a short caption for this image', and identifies the LLaVA versions used in the new experiment. Existing optimizer, learning rate, training duration, hardware and model-source information remain unchanged, as does the promise of a future code release.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive positioning against prior attacks and distillation methods are retained. Updates to MambaVision, BIA and defense references replace preprint metadata with publication information for the same works.

P1.justification: V4 makes limited terminology and punctuation edits, corrects a Table 1 pointer, removes the supplementary introduction's unresolved errata announcement, and adds several appendix discussion paragraphs. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: V4 adds Tables S9-S10, rearranges the final appendix page around the retained purification and seed tables, moves the limitations paragraph, and replaces Figure S10 with revised examples and a more explicit caption. Other figures and table structures are largely retained, with small labeling and formatting adjustments.

improvement.justification: V4 adds useful multimodal evaluations and makes Table 7's early-block cross-domain value consistent with Table 6. However, the additions introduce reporting problems: the CLIP discussion references a missing table, purification prose contradicts Table S8's ASR/FR trends, and Figure S10's 0.2 threshold conflicts with the retained zero-threshold formula. The new evaluations are also sparsely specified. These gains and new inconsistencies leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
